summary: Iteration_30 ebMS Reliable Messaging (async ACKs + duplicaatonderdrukking): compiled cleanly for cpa-service + ebms-orchestrator on JDK 17. Added 25 new Mockito-only unit tests covering CPA XML syncReplyMode parsing (6), AckSendingService fire-and-forget behaviour (3) and OrchestratorService buildInboundResponse (sync/async/fail-safe + duplicate paths) (10, includes 6 for AsyncAck flow). Updated existing InboundPipelineIntegrationTest duplicate test to no-longer expect DuplicateMessageException (Testcontainer-based, not runnable in sandbox but now correct semantics + compiles cleanly). All 107 cpa-service unit tests + 62 ebms-orchestrator unit tests pass. Only failures are the 3 known Testcontainers-based tests that require Docker (unavailable in sandbox: InboundPipelineIntegrationTest, OrchestratorServiceIntegrationTest, OutboundPipelineIntegrationTest) - same behaviour as iterations 21-29. EbmsMessageProvider no longer catches DuplicateMessageException (dead-code cleanup confirmed compiles). AsyncConfig with bounded ackTaskExecutor bean is picked up by Spring context (no bean conflict with @EnableScheduling/@EnableCaching). NOTE: real end-to-end async HTTP delivery to a live Digikoppeling/Logius partner cannot be tested in this sandbox - unit/mock-level verification of the AckSendingService call chain (createAck -> getDeliveryChannel(cpaId, fromPartyId REVERSE lookup) -> outboundSoapClient.send) is the acceptable substitute per user statement.
critical_code_review_comments: AckSendingService.sendAsyncAck() correctly performs the REVERSE lookup (fromPartyId, the original sender) - verified via Mockito.

AckSendingService fire-and-forget contract holds: both a channel-lookup failure and an outbound send failure are swallowed and logged, never propagated - this is essential because @Async(ackTaskExecutor) means the caller thread already returned; a thrown exception would only surface in the executor's error handler and could cause spurious log noise on the caller.

OrchestratorService.processInboundMessage() correctly funnels BOTH the happy path (step 9) and the DuplicateMessageException catch-block through buildInboundResponse() - duplicate now triggers a NEW async ACK-send instead of a DuplicateElimination fault (Gap 1 compliant with ebXML MSG v2.0 §7.4).

Fail-safe on isAsyncReplyMode() is correct: any exception from cpaValidationService.getDeliveryChannel() (channel not found, cpa-service down, etc.) returns false, preserving legacy synchronous ACK behaviour - critical for regression since ~47 existing test-CPAs have no syncReplyMode set.

Duplicate messages no longer republish to the AMQP inbound queue (verified in OrchestratorServiceReliableMessagingResponseTest.duplicate_doesNotRepublishToInboundQueue) - prevents double downstream delivery.
EbmsMessageProvider.invoke() no longer catches DuplicateMessageException nor imports it - clean compile confirmed, no other code path relies on that old behaviour.
AsyncConfig uses a BOUNDED ThreadPoolTaskExecutor (core=2 max=5 queue=50) instead of Spring's default unbounded SimpleAsyncTaskExecutor - protects against thread exhaustion under async-ACK bursts.
V2__add_sync_reply_mode.sql uses ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS - idempotent, does not break existing rows (nullable column, no default backfill needed).
CpaPartyXmlParser.parseDeliveryChannel() reuses the existing getLenientAttribute helper for syncReplyMode - namespace-prefix agnostic (tp:syncReplyMode works too, verified).

MINOR: AckSendingService has no unit test for the @Async wiring itself (i.e. verifying it actually runs on ackTaskExecutor rather than blocking the caller). This would require a SpringBootTest with @EnableAsync active. Given the mock-level chain is verified and the @Async('ackTaskExecutor') annotation is explicit, this is acceptable but could be added in a follow-up SpringBoot slice test.

MINOR: no explicit verification that the AsyncConfig bean loads in the Spring context. A one-liner @SpringBootTest smoke test on the orchestrator context (e.g. asserting TaskExecutor ackTaskExecutor exists) would catch bean-conflict regressions early. Not blocking - EbmsOrchestratorApplicationTests already loads the full context so any bean-conflict would surface there (currently passes).

MINOR: CpaMapper.toChannelDto uses @Mapper unmappedTargetPolicy=IGNORE which means MapStruct auto-maps syncReplyMode by name (entity field -> dto field, both String) - no explicit @Mapping needed and confirmed working via existing CpaServiceDeliveryChannelSyncTest (still passes).
